answer: In an agent market booking timber deliveries to a jetty before the tide turns, each identity must lock a $100 bond for 30 days to gain one bidding slot. The market counts only separately funded bonds, so splitting one deposit among aliases creates no extra slots. An attacker running 1,000 fake agents must therefore immobilize $100,000 for a month, sacrificing liquidity and potential returns elsewhere; generating names alone buys no influence.
